newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool futures continue to surge ahead.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool futures continue to surge ahead.

text.p: Australian wool futures prices rose further on Wednesday to continue the strong performance of futures and physical markets of recent weeks.
Traded 21-micron greasy wool futures contracts on the Sydney Futures Exchange were mostly up by eight cents to nine cents a kg clean across the range by 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT).
The nearby June contract was up by nine cents to 884 cents a kg clean on 14 lots traded.
October 1997 posted the biggest traded price rise of 12 cents to 870 cents a kg.
By 3.00 p.m. a total of 76 lots had traded, an average day for recent weeks, brokers said.
The futures market was reflecting the day's action in the physical auction market, Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures told Reuters.
"There is good demand across the board," he said.
At 3.00 p.m. the eastern market indicator at the physical auction in Sydney was up by about 10 cents a kg clean, brokers said.
This followed the indicator's rise to a 21-month high of 700 cents a kg last week.
It appeared as though finer micron wool would continue to increase in price toward the 900 cents mark, Lindsay said.
Ords' technical analysis projected Sydney Futures Exchange wool futures to hit the 900 cents mark before long, he said.
The SFE had a record total of 1,117 wool open interest positions on Wednesday.
